Topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

Target audience: Undergraduate students in STEM fields

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites & Intuition (1 Minute)

Lecture lines:
A basis is like a coordinate system.
Basis vectors define our grid.
Any vector is a linear combination.
Change perspectives, keep the vector.
How do we describe this change?

Planned animations:
Create a light blue (#87CEFA) Dot at the center.
Fade in a white (#FFFFFF) label 'Origin' near the dot.
Transform the Dot into a 2D Square with light green (#90EE90) boundary.
Highlight the Square by increasing its stroke width.
Fade out all elements to black background.

Section: section_2 — The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation (1.5 Minutes)

Lecture lines:
We map old to new coordinates.
The change-of-basis matrix is P.
P columns are new basis vectors.
Robot dogs use P to navigate.
Matrix P translates local steps globally.

Planned animations:
Draw a red (#FF6347) arrow representing Vector v on screen.
Add a blue (#4682B4) grid background behind the vector.
Rotate the grid while keeping Vector v fixed in position.
Highlight the transformation matrix M in yellow (#FFFF00).
Animate vector v coordinates shifting relative to grid rotation.

Section: section_3 — The Change-of-Basis Formula (1.5 Minutes)

Lecture lines:
Formula: v_B equals P inverse v_A.
P transforms new to old.
Inverse converts old to new.
A camera lens frame is new.
Pixels map to world view.

Planned animations:
Display the formula [P]_[B] = C^{-1} [P]_[A] in white (#FFFFFF).
Color the change-of-basis matrix C in orange (#FFA500).
Animate an arrow pointing from [P]_[A] to [P]_[B].
Flash the inverse matrix C^{-1} in light blue (#87CEFA).
Highlight the equality sign in bold green (#32CD32).

Section: section_4 — Summary & Conceptual Application (1 Minute)

Lecture lines:
The vector itself never changes.
Only its coordinate description shifts.
Key for graphics and PCA.

Planned animations:
Display summary points in a list using light gray (#D3D3D3).
Create a visual comparison of Basis A and Basis B side by side.
Animate a scaling transformation between the two bases.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
